Q: Why can't a string_view be used as a condition expression? A:

If "nullish state" is a state that is not associated with any range, then there is no such state. A range [s, s) is a valid empty range for any iterator s [1], and a null pointer is an iterator (not dereferenceable, but this is not required). So a default-constructed std::string_view is associated with an empty range of characters, and so is std::string_view(p, p) for any p, including nullptr.

It isn't clear what merit could be derived from treating an empty range based at nullptr differently from any other empty range.

Q: Jenkins with Docker, resolving agent saying : "open certs client ca.pem: no such file or directory" A:

Copy certs into jenkins-data volume

The jenkins-data volume is mounted in both jenkins-blueocean (/var/jenkins_home) and accessible from DinD. After DinD generates certs, copy the client certs into the jenkins-data volume so agents can reach them from a path that DinD manages.

Add this to your jenkins-docker service:

jenkins-docker:
  ...
  volumes:
    - jenkins-docker-certs:/certs/client
    - jenkins-data:/var/jenkins_home
  entrypoint: >
    sh -c "
      dockerd-entrypoint.sh --storage-driver=overlay2 &
      until [ -f /certs/client/ca.pem ]; do sleep 1; done;
      cp /certs/client/* /var/jenkins_home/certs/
      wait
    "

Then in your agent template, set DOCKER_CERT_PATH=/var/jenkins_home/certs — since jenkins-data is mounted the same way in both controller and agents, this path resolves correctly inside DinD-spawned containers.
